The rules were in the reports app's `reports.scss` and never matched because their selectors had no `:global()`. PR #358 (ticket O3-5965) removed them as dead code, so nothing changed visually.

**Why they could never match.** The reports app's stylesheets are CSS Modules. Without `:global()`, a selector like `.cds--date-picker` gets rewritten to a module-scoped hashed class name, so it never matches Carbon's real class names in the rendered markup. The four rules were `width: 100%` on `.cds--date-picker`, `.cds--select`, `.cds--select-input` and `.cds--date-picker__input`, nested under `.filterForm .formField` (the filter form's field wrapper). The PR description says they "have never had any effect" (`openmrs-esm-admin-tools/packages/esm-reports-app/src/components/reports.scss`, removed in `fbda030`; the removed block sat around lines 117–138 of the prior version). The current file still has the `.filterForm` block (lines 104–130) without those rules.

**What was done.** PR #358 (`(chore) O3-5965: Remove inert Carbon CSS rules from reports app`, merged 2026-10-01 by solomonfortune, approved by denniskigen) deleted the four rules. It was a behavior-preserving cleanup: the author verified with a grep showing no `cds--` names left in the file, a passing production build, and unchanged tests. No new tests were added. The related commit `feb0ba0` removed 13 other unused CSS Module classes from the same app.

**Context.** The date picker in the run-report form had already moved to `OpenmrsDatePicker` in PR #72 (`9ccfccb`). Later, PR #423 (`827b70e`) replaced the fixed-width selects and per-field margins with a Carbon `Stack`, so the fields became full width by a different route. I did not find any commit that made the removed selectors work, and I did not run the build or check the rendered DOM myself. The explanation of the CSS Modules behaviour comes from the PR description and the code.
